html:
A Chinese e-commerce company founded in 1999 in Hangzhou by Jack Ma, a former English teacher, and a small group of partners. It began as a website linking Chinese factories with buyers abroad.

China's entry into the world trade system (joining the WTO in 2001) and the spread of the internet gave it room to grow. Its consumer site Taobao, launched in 2003, drove eBay out of China. Alipay, its payment service, solved the problem of trust between strangers buying online and grew into Ant Group. Alibaba's Singles' Day sales each November became the biggest shopping event in the world.

Its listing in New York in 2014 raised about 25 billion dollars, then a record. In 2020, after Ma criticised regulators, the government halted Ant Group's share sale, and in 2021 fined Alibaba for abusing its market power. The episode showed the limits that Xi Jinping's government set on private tech giants.
